steps.purpose: Correct the public product model around conversational roadmap control.

steps.thought: The roadmap MCP explicitly says roadmap_reprioritize records a re-prioritization proposal and does not reorder the roadmap; re-prioritization stays a human decision. The user drives direction by talking to the agent, then directs the accepted update.

steps.purpose: ts1 open: shape the in-process think-and-ship adoption
steps.context: Run of ts1→ts2, wb1→wb2/wb3. Refresh #2 committed as 60e7d55. Grounded both crates: think-and-ship 0.5.0 (local checkout clean at tag v0.5.0 = crates.io) exposes RoadmapEngine/ShipEngine/ReasoningServer/SignalEngine builders with with_persistence + with_broadcaster; infra::Persistence(Domain) + PersistenceConfig::from_env (THINK_AND_SHIP_PERSIST/DATA_DIR); project identity via resolve_project_id_with(None, cwd) reading .think-and-ship/project.json; Broadcaster is an NDJSON unix socket bound only when THINK_AND_SHIP_BROADCAST_PATH is set. Magistr: engine crate is pure domain; EngineHandle composes RoadmapManager (progress only) and nobody currently feeds update_roadmap_progress; EngineHandle constructed in server/main.rs and gui workflow.rs; ProjectConfig canonical in magistr-core (src/core/types re-exports it).
steps.thought: Landmine 1 dissolves: magistr's Cargo.lock has zero rmcp — src/mcp_tools is a hand-rolled JSON-RPC loop — so think-and-ship's rmcp 3.0.0-beta.2 lands with no reconciliation; cost is build weight (axum, reqwest-rustls, tungstenite) which the decision already accepted. Dep form: crates.io "0.5.0" because the checkout is at that exact tag; a commented [patch.crates-io] block in the workspace root is the path override for when the library moves ahead. Shape: engine/src/tas/ (one pub item per file): TasConfig (data_dir from env chain, persistence ON unless THINK_AND_SHIP_PERSIST is explicitly false — a native subsystem that forgets by default is useless, but DATA_DIR/explicit-off semantics are honoured), identity (ensure_project_file(root) writes .think-and-ship/project.json with the id the root already resolves to — never mint), NativeEngines (Arc<Mutex<>> per engine, shared Persistence per Domain, typed commands: roadmap next/status/start/complete/snapshot, think record_step/pin, ship set_objective/add_task/start/record_action/record_check(with real exit code)/complete/finalize, signal capture), progress_from_roadmap (chunks→RoadmapProgress: tasks = non-obsoleted chunks, checked = done, phases = groups), NativeRoadmapSnapshot (counts, next ready, regions), NativeFrame (family/type/payload parsed from a broadcast line), subscriber (connect unix socket, read lines, hand NativeFrame to EngineHandle). EngineHandle gets an Option<NativeEngines> outside the state mutex, with_native(), native(), refresh_native_roadmap() feeding RoadmapManager, and EngineEvent::Native(NativeFrame). ThinkEngine is ReasoningServer::new_for_project(config, id) with Persistence::for_project — same file as the external server. Two-writer safety is the library's locked merge; test it with two RoadmapEngine instances on a temp data dir.
steps.outcome: Plan fixed: 5 ship tasks (dep, native module, handle+subscriber, wiring+flag+init, verify). No user decision needed for ts1; the ts2 mounting strategy (rmcp rewrite vs delegate into UnifiedService) is the fork to raise later.
steps.next_action: Add the dependency and confirm the workspace builds before writing any tas code.
steps.rationale: Dep resolution is the only step that can fail for reasons outside my control (registry, MSRV, feature unification); proving it first keeps the probe chunk honest.

steps.purpose: ts2b close: skills, templates and tool guide on think-and-ship; magistr_roadmap_* removed
steps.context: Chunk 1 of the 2026-08-26 run (ts2b → ts3 → ts4). Opened at think:17.
steps.thought: Shipped as planned, one commit. Findings worth keeping: (1) The "no magistr_roadmap_* string remains" bullet is met everywhere except ROADMAP.md, which is a generated view of chunk descriptions that legitimately narrate the removal — exempted, not scrubbed. (2) CLAUDE.md is NeverOverwrite, so the think-and-ship section is a post-step splice (upsert_claude_md_section) that keeps the user's text and reports CLAUDE.md as `updated` only when the block changed; three preserve-tests were relaxed from byte-equality to "starts with the user's text, then the marked block". The splice reproduces think-and-ship init's markers and body byte-for-byte, so either tool can refresh it — including the legacy unterminated block, bounded at the next `# ` heading. (3) ROADMAP_MUTATION_SUFFIXES now names the think-and-ship mutating verbs (+ signal_promote); the TUI SetRoadmapStale flag and the GUI data-changed emission therefore keep firing on the new tools without any consumer change. (4) `magistr roadmap generate` was the anticipated fork; it resolved as a prompt rewrite (roadmap_add_chunk with content/group/deps/priority bands, research recorded in think) with the CLI's agent-session flow untouched — ts4 still owns show/next/export. (5) The vendored skills name ministr_*/serpapi; a footer note routes those to workbench/web search. The pin is a vendoring date because ~/.claude/skills is not a git checkout. (6) Honest gap: the engine's plan-file guard still demands .magistr/current-plan.md, which the new skills no longer write; ts2c (deps ts2b, now ready) keys the guards on ship state. Until then a `magistr next` run hits the guard's "write a plan" message once. (7) svelte-check: 1 pre-existing error (dag.test.ts cannot resolve vitest types), none from the prompt-string edits. Subsumption: ts4's "`generate` re-implemented as AI-authored chunks via roadmap_add_chunk" bullet is done by this chunk.
steps.outcome: ts2b done (8482 tests, all four gates exit 0). ts4's generate bullet subsumed; ts2c became ready and is the natural next chunk, but the run's explicit order continues with ts3.
steps.next_action: Between-chunk step: roadmap_update_chunk(ts4) to drop the generate bullet; re-derive the frontier; start ts3-gui-roadmap.
steps.rationale: The chunk was wide but mechanical once the replacement vocabulary was fixed; the only judgment calls (generate scope, CLAUDE.md splice policy, ROADMAP.md exemption) are recorded here so the next run does not re-derive them.
